page: The Amazon Web Services r8gb.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture. The system is equipped with 16 dedicated physical cores based on the AWS Neoverse-V2 processor family running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz, with single-threaded execution per core and no simultaneous multithreading. Cache resources include 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of dedicated L2 cache per core, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache pool. System memory is configured at 128 GB, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8 GB per vCPU.

Hardware accelerators such as GPUs are not present on this instance, and it does not include bundled local instance storage, requiring remote storage volumes over the Nitro architecture for persistent disk operations. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth capacity of 33 Gbps, delivering strong networking throughput for distributed services.

Benchmark results highlight notable strengths in memory throughput and data manipulation tasks. Memory benchmarking demonstrates top-tier performance on the PassMark memory evaluation and strong results in uncached 256 MB read and write memory bandwidth. Decompression workloads via multi-threaded bzip3 and relational operations in PassMark database benchmarks also place in the upper quartile. Conversely, general CPU benchmarks such as Geekbench and stress-ng place in the median range, while large language model text generation scores drop significantly due to CPU-bound execution without hardware acceleration.

The r8gb.4xlarge provides high memory density per physical core combined with modern ARM architectural efficiencies, making it cost-efficient for memory-sensitive configurations compared to standard x86 compute instances. It is best suited for in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, distributed memory computing, extract-transform-load (ETL) data pipelines, and database processing tasks.
description: The Amazon Web Services r8gb.4xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server based on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.8 GHz, with 128 GB of system memory providing an 8 GB per vCPU allocation. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage while offering a 33 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks indicate top-tier memory subsystem performance and strong uncached read and write throughput, alongside upper-quartile database operation metrics. General integer and floating-point compute benchmarks register at median cloud averages, with lower relative output during intensive language model inference tasks. The r8gb.4xlarge offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for memory-heavy enterprise deployments, making it well matched for in-memory key-value stores, distributed caches, high-concurrency database workloads, and large-scale data processing pipelines.
